title: Mechanistic insights into Moringa oleifera leaf bioactive against cytotoxic stress: an integrative approach.
authors: Richards, Vivianna James; Rowland, Ryan Mathew; Thilipkumar, Lekha Priya; Balaji, Priyanka; Bhoothakallu Lolajaksha, Amshumala; Gnanasekaran, Tamizh Selvan; Kuppusamy, Vijayalakshmi; Jagannathan, Vijayalakshmi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究辣木叶提取物对DNA损伤的辐射防护作用，分子对接与MD模拟聚焦于Kaempferol与Keap1-Nrf2蛋白复合物，而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Exposure to ionizing radiation during medical diagnostics and cancer therapy often results in collateral damage to healthy cells, primarily due to the generation of free radicals. Moringa oleifera (MO), known for its rich antioxidant profile, may offer protective effects against such damage. This study investigates the radioprotective potential of MO leaf extract against DNA damage induced by bleomycin and X-irradiation. The antioxidant capacity of the extract was evaluated using DPPH radical scavenging assays, which revealed a dose-dependent increase in free radical inhibition, from 21.51% at 0.2 mg/mL to 51.07% at 1 mg/mL. UV-Vis spectral analysis showed strong absorbance around 370 nm, indicating the presence of flavonoid compounds. HPLC profiling further confirmed the phytochemical composition, with prominent peaks corresponding to kaempferol and related flavonoids, indicating their substantial abundance in the extract. In vitro experiments using human peripheral blood lymphocytes treated with MO demonstrated a significant (p < 0.0001) reduction in chromosomal aberrations and DNA strand breaks following exposure to bleomycin (40 microg/mL) and X-irradiation (2 Gy). Furthermore, molecular docking and 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations revealed that kaempferol, a major MO constituent, exhibited strong binding affinity with the Keap1-Nrf2 complex, suggesting activation of antioxidant gene expression. Overall, the findings support MO's role as a natural, low-toxicity radioprotective agent and highlight the complementary value of computational approaches alongside cytogenetic assays in validating therapeutic potential.
abstract_zh: 在医学诊断和癌症治疗过程中暴露于电离辐射常因自由基的产生而对健康细胞造成附带损伤。辣木 (Moringa oleifera, MO) 以其丰富的抗氧化特性著称，可能对此类损伤提供保护作用。本研究探讨了MO叶提取物对博来霉素和X射线照射诱导的DNA损伤的辐射防护潜力。通过DPPH自由基清除实验评估提取物的抗氧化能力，结果显示自由基抑制呈剂量依赖性增加，从0.2 mg/mL时的21.51%升至1 mg/mL时的51.07%。UV-Vis光谱分析显示在约370 nm处有强吸收，表明存在黄酮类化合物。HPLC分析进一步确认了植物化学成分，其中突出的峰对应山柰酚及相关黄酮类化合物，表明这些成分在提取物中含量丰富。使用人外周血淋巴细胞进行的体外实验显示，经MO处理后，博来霉素（40微克/mL）和X射线照射（2 Gy）诱导的染色体畸变和DNA链断裂显著减少（p < 0.0001）。此外，分子对接和200 ns分子动力学模拟揭示，MO的主要成分山柰酚与Keap1-Nrf2复合物表现出强结合亲和力，提示其可能激活抗氧化基因表达。总体而言，这些发现支持MO作为天然、低毒性的辐射防护剂的作用，并强调了计算方法与细胞遗传学检测在验证治疗潜力方面的互补价值。
